functions.name: ProcessLevelSubTiles
functions.comment:
Initializes and executes level sub-tile processing context for automap generation.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve LvlSubTxt pointer from level object at offset 0x218
2. Zero-initialize 14-element context array (0x38 bytes total)
3. Set up pointers to sub-tile data regions (offsets 0x04, 0x2c, 0x54)
4. Configure operation parameters (preset ID, mode, direction mask)
5. Assign callback function pointers for tile processing operations
6. Invoke sub-tile processor FUN_6fdd4a40 with populated context

Parameters:
  nPresetId (int): Preset identifier/orientation index (0-3 typical)
  nOperationMode (int): Processing mode (4=standard, 799=expanded)
  IMPLICIT in_EAX: Pointer to level/room object containing LvlSubTxt at +0x218

Returns:
  void - Results applied through callback functions

Structure Layout (Context on Stack):
  Offset  Size  Field               Description
  0x00    4     pLevel              Level object pointer (in_EAX)
  0x04    4     pSubTileData54      Ptr to LvlSubTxt+0x54
  0x08    4     pSubTileData04      Ptr to LvlSubTxt+0x04
  0x0C    4     pSubTileData2C      Ptr to LvlSubTxt+0x2C
  0x10    4     nMode               Operation mode from param_2
  0x14    4     nDirectionMask      Direction mask (-1 = all directions)
  0x18    4     nPreset             Preset ID from param_1
  0x1C    4     pfnCheckWalkable    Callback: FUN_6fd85000 - checks cell visibility
  0x20    4     pfnValidateBounds   Callback: FUN_6fd85720 - validates area bounds
  0x28    4     pfnSetFlags1        Callback: FUN_6fd85080 - sets dword flags
  0x2C    4     pfnSetFlags2        Callback: FUN_6fd85030 - sets dword flags
  0x30    4     pfnApplyPreset      Callback: FUN_6fd858f0 - applies preset to cells

Callers:
  FUN_6fd9a640 - Level rendering with orientations 0-3, mode 4
  FUN_6fdd5c30 - Special level processing with mode 799
  FUN_6fdd5870 - Additional level sub-tile processing

functions.name: PlacePresetInRandomCell
functions.comment:
Places a preset in a random valid cell within the room using Fisher-Yates shuffle.

Algorithm:
1. Calculates total interior cells as (width-2) * (height-2)
2. Creates array of cell coordinates, excluding 1-cell border
3. Shuffles cell array using Linear Congruential Generator (LCG) RNG
4. For each shuffled cell, checks if flag 0x80 is set (preset-allowed marker)
5. If allowed, tests 8 neighboring directions using offset tables
6. On first valid neighbor position, places preset and returns success
7. If no cells accept preset, falls back to FUN_6fd85a80

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT in_EAX - Pointer to room/level generation context
    +0x218: Pointer to RoomData structure
    +0x1f8: LCG state low DWORD (seed)
    +0x1fc: LCG state high DWORD (carry)
  nPresetId (stack) - Preset type ID to place (from LvlPrest.txt)
  nParam2 (stack) - Secondary parameter (likely spawn flags or -1 for default)

Returns:
  1 - Preset was successfully placed
  0 - No valid placement found (room too small or all cells invalid)

Magic Numbers:
  0x6ac690c5 - LCG multiplier for random number generation
  0x80 - Cell flag indicating preset placement is allowed
  0x0f - Direction flags mask (all 4 cardinal + 4 diagonal)
  8 - Number of neighbor directions checked

RoomData Structure Layout (at in_EAX+0x218):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  +0x2c   4     pCellFlags      Pointer to cell flag array
  +0x30   4     pRowOffsets     Pointer to row offset table
  +0x5c   4     nWidth          Room width in cells
  +0x60   4     nHeight         Room height in cells

functions.name: LoadAutomapTxtData
functions.comment:
Loads and parses automap.txt data file, building the automap records table.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize automap status structure (set type to 0x29A)
2. Build column descriptor array for 11 columns (LevelName, TileName, Style, 
   StartSequence, EndSequence, Cel1-Cel4, Waypoint, SoundEnv)
3. Call DATATBLS_LoadTextFile to parse automap.txt using column descriptors
4. Allocate memory for automap records array (nRecords * 0x20 bytes per record)
5. Zero-initialize the allocated memory using REP STOSD/STOSB
6. For each raw text record:
   a. Call LookupLevelNameIndex to convert level name string to index
   b. Call LookupTileCodeIndex to convert tile code string to index
   c. Copy style byte, sequence bytes, and cel indices (4 dwords)
   d. Count valid cel entries (non -1 values) and store count
   e. Skip records with no valid cels
7. Free the raw text data buffer
8. Store g_pAutomapRecords and g_nAutomapRecordCount globals
9. Initialize level index lookup tables (g_anAutomapLevelStartIndices/EndIndices)
   to -1 for all 36 possible levels
10. Build level-to-record index mapping by iterating records and grouping
    by level ID, storing start/end indices for each level

Parameters:
  nUnused (ECX): Unused parameter (always 0 from caller)
  pMemPool (EDX): Memory pool context for allocation

Returns:
  void - Results stored in globals

Globals Written:
  g_pAutomapStatusStruct[0] = 0
  g_pAutomapStatusStruct[4] = 0x29A (automap type ID)
  g_pAutomapRecords = Pointer to allocated automap record array
  g_nAutomapRecordCount = Number of valid automap records
  g_anAutomapLevelStartIndices[0..35] = First record index for each level
  g_anAutomapLevelEndIndices[0..35] = Last record index + 1 for each level

Automap Record Structure (0x20 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x00    4     nLevelIndex     Level name lookup index
  0x04    4     nTileCodeIndex  Tile code lookup index
  0x08    1     bStyle          Automap style byte
  0x09    1     bStartSeq       Start sequence value
  0x0A    1     bEndSeq         End sequence value
  0x0B    1     bPadding        Unused padding
  0x0C    4     nCel1           Cel frame index 1 (-1 if unused)
  0x10    4     nCel2           Cel frame index 2 (-1 if unused)
  0x14    4     nCel3           Cel frame index 3 (-1 if unused)
  0x18    4     nCel4           Cel frame index 4 (-1 if unused)
  0x1C    4     nValidCelCount  Count of valid cel entries (0-4)

Error Handling:
  0x51E - Record has no valid cel entries (skipped, not fatal)
  0x539 - Level index overflow during index table build (fatal)

Magic Numbers:
  0x29A = Automap data type identifier
  0x20 = Size of each automap record structure
  0x2C = Size of raw text record from parser
  0x508 = Pool allocation identifier for automap records
  36 = Maximum number of levels (loop from 0x6FDEFE34 to 0x6FDEFF54)

functions.name: LoadLevelWarpTable
functions.comment:
Loads the Level Warp data table from lvlwarp.txt.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize array of 12 FormatDescriptor entries on stack
2. Configure field descriptors for all 11 LvlWarp columns:
   - SelectX/Y: Warp selection coordinates (offsets 0x00-0x04)
   - SelectDX/DY: Selection delta/dimensions (offsets 0x08-0x0C)
   - ExitWalkX/Y: Exit walk position (offsets 0x10-0x14)
   - OffsetX/Y: Display offset coordinates (offsets 0x18-0x1C)
   - LitVersion: Lighting version flag (offset 0x20)
   - Tiles: Number of tiles (offset 0x24)
   - Direction: Warp direction (offset 0x28)
3. Add terminator entry with g_aFieldDescriptorEnd
4. Call DATATBLS_LoadTextFile to parse lvlwarp.txt
5. Store result pointer in g_pLevelWarpTable
6. Store record count in g_dwLevelWarpCount

Parameters:

  szArchiveName (EDX): Archive name containing the text file

Returns:
  void - Results stored in global variables

Globals Modified:
  g_pLevelWarpTable: Pointer to loaded LvlWarp record array
  g_dwLevelWarpCount: Number of records loaded

Structure Layout (LvlWarpRecord, 0x30 bytes per entry):
  Offset  Size  Field        Description
  0x00    4     SelectX      Selection X coordinate
  0x04    4     SelectY      Selection Y coordinate
  0x08    4     SelectDX     Selection width/delta X
  0x0C    4     SelectDY     Selection height/delta Y
  0x10    4     ExitWalkX    Exit walk target X
  0x14    4     ExitWalkY    Exit walk target Y
  0x18    4     OffsetX      Display offset X
  0x1C    4     OffsetY      Display offset Y
  0x20    4     LitVersion   Lighting version
  0x24    4     Tiles        Number of tiles
  0x28    4     Direction    Warp direction
  0x2C    4     Reserved     Padding to 0x30

functions.name: LoadLevelTypesData
functions.comment:
Loads and initializes level types data from the lvltypes.txt text file.

Algorithm:
1. Construct stack-based FormatDescriptor array describing 35 fields:
   - File 1-32: String fields for tile file paths (each 0x3b=59 chars)
   - MonPreset fields reference via g_aMonPresetFormatFields
   - Expansion: Boolean field
   - End marker via g_aFieldDescriptorEnd
2. Call DATATBLS_LoadTextFile to parse lvltypes.txt into record array
3. Store result pointer in g_pLevelTypesData global
4. Store record count in g_nLevelTypesCount global
5. For each loaded level type record:
   - Execute inner loop 32 times (once per File slot)
   - Call FUN_6fd86980 with tiles path to initialize tile data

Parameters:
- pMemPool: Memory pool allocator for data table allocation

Returns:

Magic Numbers:
- 0x3b (59): Field size for file path strings
- 0x788 (1928): Total record size in bytes
- 0x20 (32): Number of tile file slots per level type
- Field offsets: 0x00, 0x3c, 0x78... incrementing by 0x3c (60) per file slot

Related Globals:
- g_pLevelTypesData (0x6fdf1424): Pointer to loaded level types array
- g_nLevelTypesCount (0x6fdf1430): Number of level type records loaded
- g_aMonPresetFormatFields: Format descriptor for monster preset fields
- g_aFieldDescriptorEnd: End-of-array sentinel marker

functions.name: LoadLevelsTxtData
functions.comment:
Loads and initializes the levels.txt data table from the game's data files.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize FormatDescriptor header with type descriptor pointer
2. Build field descriptor array on stack (141 columns defining level properties)
3. Call DATATBLS_LoadTextFile to parse "levels.txt" into g_pLevelsTxtRecords
4. Validate record count does not exceed 1024 (0x400) entries
5. For each level record:
   a. Zero-initialize monster arrays at offsets 0x16E and 0x1BE (20 DWORDs each)
   b. Copy level name strings with null termination
   c. Count valid monsters in mon1-mon25, nmon1-nmon25, umon1-umon25 arrays
   d. Store counts at offsets 0x33, 0x34, 0x35 respectively

Parameters:
  pMemPool - void* Memory pool for allocation (passed to DATATBLS_LoadTextFile)

Returns:
  void - Data stored in globals g_pLevelsTxtRecords and g_dwLevelsTxtRecordCount

Stack Variables Note:
  The ~570 local_ variables are the field descriptor array (141 entries x 5 DWORDs each).
  These represent compile-time constants for column definitions, not runtime variables.
  Each 20-byte field descriptor: szName, dwType, dwFlags, dwOffset, pLookupTable.

Field Descriptor Format (20 bytes each):
  Offset 0x00: char* szColumnName - Column name in text file
  Offset 0x04: dword dwType - Data type (2=short, 3=ushort, 4=byte, 0x14=lookup)
  Offset 0x08: dword dwFlags - Processing flags
  Offset 0x0C: dword dwOffset - Byte offset in output record structure
  Offset 0x10: void* pLookupTable - Pointer to lookup table (for type 0x14)

LevelsTxt Record Structure Size: 0x220 (544 bytes)

Key Columns Parsed:
  MonLvl1-3, MonLvl1Ex-3Ex - Monster level settings
  MonDen, MonDen(N), MonDen(H) - Monster density per difficulty
  MonUMin/Max - Unique monster min/max counts
  mon1-25, nmon1-25, umon1-25 - Monster type arrays (normal/nightmare/unique)
  ObjGrp0-7, ObjPrb0-7 - Object group and probability settings
  LevelName, LevelWarp, EntryFile - Level identification strings

Magic Numbers:
  0x400 (1024) - Maximum allowed level record count
  0x220 (544) - Size of each LevelsTxt record in bytes
  0x16E (366) - Offset to first monster preset array
  0x1BE (446) - Offset to second monster preset array
  0x14 (20) - Number of DWORDs in each monster array
  0x19 (25) - Maximum monsters per array (mon1-mon25)
  0xC7 (199) - Error line number for abort

Error Handling:
  If record count exceeds 1024, calls CleanupAndAbort with line 199

External Calls:
  DATATBLS_LoadTextFile - Parse text file into record array
  Ordinal_10002 (Fog_GetStringFromOffset) - Get string pointer from data offset
  strncpy - Copy level name strings with length limit

functions.name: LoadLevelSubstitutionTable
functions.signature: void LoadLevelSubstitutionTable(void * this, void * pMemPool, int nLoadMode, int nExpansionFlag)
functions.comment:
Loads the Level Substitution (lvlsub.txt) data table and initializes related structures.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize FormatDescriptor array with 23 field definitions for parsing lvlsub.txt
2. Call DATATBLS_LoadTextFile to parse lvlsub.txt into g_pLvlSubTxt array
3. Find maximum Type value across all records (stride 0x57 dwords per record)
4. Allocate index table g_pLvlSubIndexTable sized to max Type value
5. Build lookup index mapping Type values to record indices
6. If nLoadMode is 0 (client mode):
   - Initialize critical section g_pLvlSubCriticalSection for thread safety
   - Skip cache allocation if nExpansionFlag is also 0
7. Allocate g_pLvlSubDataCache array for processed level substitution data
8. Validate D2Exp.mpq presence and load DT1 tile data for each record

Parameters:
pMemPool     - IMPLICIT in ECX, memory pool for allocation tracking
nLoadMode   - Load mode flag (0=client, non-zero=server)
nExpansionFlag - Expansion mode flag (controls cache allocation)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Aborts with line 0x3B6 if critical section already initialized
- Aborts with line 0x3D1 if DT1 tile data fails to load (offset 0x4C == 0)

Magic Numbers:
0x57  - Stride between lvlsub records (87 dwords = 348 bytes)
0x15c - Record size passed to DATATBLS_LoadTextFile (348 bytes)
0x3a6 - Line number for index table allocation
0x3b6 - Line number for critical section error
0x3b8 - Line number for critical section allocation
0x3be - Line number for data cache allocation
0x3d1 - Line number for DT1 load failure

functions.name: LoadLevelPresetData
functions.comment:
Loads and parses lvlprest.txt data table for level preset configurations.

Algorithm:
1. Build a FormatDescriptor array (26 entries) defining all lvlprest.txt columns
2. Call DATATBLS_LoadTextFile to parse lvlprest.txt into g_pLvlPrestData
3. If nLoadExpansionTiles is set, allocate tile reference storage array
4. Check if D2Exp.mpq expansion is available via FindAndValidateD2ExpMpq
5. Iterate through all level preset records
6. For each record, skip if expansion-only and expansion not available
7. Process 6 tile files (File1-File6) per preset record
8. Register tile files with FUN_6fd86980 for tile loading
9. If loading expansion tiles, calculate string length and call FUN_6fdd2a20

Parameters:
  pMemPool - Memory pool for data allocation (passed to DATATBLS_LoadTextFile)
  nLoadExpansionTiles - If non-zero, allocate and populate tile reference array

Returns:
  void (data stored in globals g_pLvlPrestData, g_pLvlPrestTileRefs)

LvlPrest Record Structure (0x1B0 = 432 bytes per record):
  Offset 0x00: Def (definition name)
  Offset 0x04: LevelId
  Offset 0x08: Populate
  Offset 0x0C: Logicals
  Offset 0x10: Outdoors
  Offset 0x14: Animate
  Offset 0x18: KillEdge
  Offset 0x1C: FillBlanks
  Offset 0x20: Expansion flag
  Offset 0x28: SizeX
  Offset 0x2C: SizeY
  Offset 0x30: AutoMap
  Offset 0x34: Scan
  Offset 0x38: Pops
  Offset 0x3C: PopPad
  Offset 0x40: Files (count)
  Offset 0x44: File1 (0x3B bytes each, 6 files)
  Offset 0x1AC: Dt1Mask

Magic Numbers:
  0x1B0 (432) - Size of one LvlPresetRecord
  0x2A7 (679) - Memory allocation ID for tile references
  0x18 (24) - Size of tile reference entry per record
  0x6 - Number of tile files per preset (File1-File6)
  0x3B (59) - Max filename length for each File field
  0x3C (60) - Stride between file entries (padded)
  0x6C (108) - Offset to next record's file section

functions.name: SortTextEntriesByKey
functions.comment:
Sorts an array of text entries using insertion sort algorithm with a custom comparator.

Algorithm:
1. Exit early if count (in_AX) is 1 or less
2. Initialize with first element as sorted portion
3. For each unsorted element (starting from second):
   a. Load current element key (wCurrentKey) and data (dwCurrentData)
   b. Call comparison function with current vs element being examined
   c. If comparison > 0: shift larger elements right and insert current
   d. Move to next unsorted element
4. Each entry is 12 bytes: 2-byte key + 4-byte data + 6-byte padding

Parameters:
  pEntryArray - Pointer to array of 12-byte text entries to sort in-place
  pfnCompare - Comparison function pointer: int __fastcall(ushort*, ushort*)
               Returns > 0 if first param should sort after second
  IMPLICIT in_AX - Number of elements in the array (ushort count)

Returns:
  void - Array is sorted in-place

Special Cases:
- If in_AX <= 1, returns immediately (nothing to sort)
- Comparison function is called repeatedly during inner loop shifts

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 12 (0xC) - Size of each entry in bytes
- 6 - Element stride in ushort units (12/2)

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field       Type        Description
------  ----  ----------  ----------  --------------------------
0x00    2     wKey        ushort      Sort key for comparison
0x02    4     dwData      uint        Associated data value/pointer
0x06    6     padding     -           Alignment/next element

- Ordinal_10102 (0x6fd8b410) - Text sorting in D2Common

functions.name: ProcessDrlgVerificationSegments
functions.signature: void ProcessDrlgVerificationSegments(uint dwUnused, int * pCoordData, int * pDefaultCoords, byte bSegmentType, DrlgVerifyEntry * pVerifyList)
functions.comment:
Processes DRLG verification segments for dungeon level generation.
Iterates through a linked list of verification entries, checking coordinate
boundaries against four directional cases and allocating new verification
nodes when segments need extension or splitting.

Algorithm:
  1. Extract 3 levels of coordinate data from pCoordData chain via [+0x10]
  2. Loop through pVerifyList linked list (next pointer at +0x14)
  3. For each entry, get coordinate node from +0x10 or use pDefaultCoords
  4. Switch on type field (+0x4) for direction:
     Case 0: Vertical down (Y axis, direction=-1)
     Case 1: Horizontal right (X axis, direction=+1)
     Case 2: Vertical up (Y axis, direction=+1)
     Case 3: Horizontal left (X axis, direction=-1)
  5. Calculate scaled segment bounds using direction multiplier
  6. If segment start within bounds, set flags on target node
  7. If segment extends past bounds, allocate new 0x14-byte node

Parameters:
  dwUnused       - uint              - Unused parameter (always ignored)
  pCoordData     - int*              - Root coordinate structure chain via [+0x10]
  pDefaultCoords - int*              - Fallback coordinates when entry has none
  bSegmentType   - byte              - Type value written to new nodes at +0x8
  pVerifyList    - DrlgVerifyEntry*  - Linked list of verification entries

Returns:
  void - No return value

Flags at offset +0xC on target node:
  0x1 - Segment verified
  0x2 - Entry has additional data (when +0x8 != 0)

Error Handling:
  Invalid type (>3) triggers CleanupAndAbort with error code 0x6D (109)

functions.name: SelectWeightedRandomTileIndex
functions.comment:
Selects a weighted random tile index from available tile options using PRNG.

Algorithm:
1. Extract tile style (bits 20-25) and tile subtype (bits 8-15) from dwTileType
2. Call Ordinal_10066 to get available tile options into local buffer (max 0x28 entries)
3. If no options found with style/subtype, retry with default parameters (style=0, subtype=0, type=0xA)
4. Iterate through options, summing weights via Ordinal_10028 (GetTileWeight)
5. If total weight is zero, return 0 (no valid selection)
6. Update PRNG state at pRoom+0xD4/0xD8 using multiplier 0x6AC690C5
7. Calculate random index using modulo or bitwise AND (power-of-2 optimization)
8. Walk through options again, subtracting weights until random threshold reached
9. Return selected tile index from options array

Parameters:
    this (ECX): IMPLICIT - Pointer to room/DRLG context structure
    dwTileType: Packed tile type descriptor
        Bits 20-25: Tile style index (0-63)
        Bits 8-15: Tile subtype index
        Other bits: Flags for tile selection

Returns:
    uint: Selected tile index from weighted random selection, or 0 if no valid tiles

Special Cases:
    If Ordinal_10066 returns 0 entries with style/subtype, retries with defaults
    Power-of-2 weight sums use fast AND masking instead of division
    Calls CleanupAndAbort if null tile entry encountered in options

Magic Numbers:
    0x6AC690C5: PRNG multiplier (LCG algorithm)
    0x28: Maximum tile options buffer size (40 entries)
    0x73, 0x7C: Source line numbers for error reporting

Structure Layout (Room at this/ESI):
    Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
    0x3C    4     pTileData       void*   Tile data pointer
    0xD4    4     dwPrngStateLo   uint    PRNG state low dword
    0xD8    4     dwPrngStateHi   uint    PRNG state high dword

functions.name: EncodeUnitDataToBitBuffer
functions.signature: void EncodeUnitDataToBitBuffer(int * pUnit, int * pBitBuffer, int nIncludeExtended, int nSaveMode)
functions.comment:
Encodes unit data into a bit buffer for network transmission or save file serialization.

This function serializes a game unit's properties into a compact bitstream format. It handles
different unit types (items, monsters, players) with type-specific encoding paths. The encoded
data includes coordinates, mode, quality, durability, stats, name, and state lists.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer and type (must be type 4 = Item)
2. Encode base unit properties: level (10 bits), mode (3 bits)
3. Encode position/dimension data based on mode (3/5 vs others)
4. If save mode (nSaveMode), write GUID and return early
5. Encode extended properties: difficulty (3 bits), level requirement (7 bits), quality (4 bits)
6. Encode quality-dependent fields (socketed, set item info)
7. Encode durability data based on item sub-type (switch on ItemData.dwType)
8. Encode special flags: runeword owner, personalization, item name
9. Encode equipped location and ownership information
10. Encode stat modifiers (experience bonus, skill bonuses)
11. Encode state lists (auras, buffs) with stat values

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to unit structure (must be type 4 = Item); pUnit[5] = ItemData pointer
  pBitBuffer - Pointer to bit buffer for output encoding via EncodeBitsToFilterBuffer
  nIncludeExtended - If nonzero, include extended data (ownership, state lists, equipped info)
  nSaveMode - If nonzero, use save-file format (writes GUID only, early return)

Returns:
  void - Function does not return a value.
  On error, calls CleanupAndAbort/ReportError and does not return.

Error Codes:
  0x1505 - Null unit pointer passed
  0x1506 - Invalid unit type (expected 4, Item type)
  0x1508 - Null ItemData pointer (pUnit[5] == 0)
  0x0923 - Failed to get item type record from Ordinal_10600

Bit Encoding Summary:
  Level: 10 bits (max 0x3FF)
  Mode: 3 bits (max 7)
  Quality: 4 bits (max 0xF)
  Durability: varies by type (4-16 bits)
  Stat ID: 9 bits (0x1FF = terminator)
  Position: 11 bits each (max 0x7FF)

  sgptDataTables - Item statistics table base
  g_adwStatListTypeIds - State list type ID mapping array (5 elements)
  g_adwCrtDataBlock_15, _20, _30 - Experience calculation blocks

functions.name: CalculateItemValue
functions.signature: int CalculateItemValue(int * pUnit, int nItemSlot, int * pInventory, int nDifficulty, int nValueMode)
functions.comment:
Calculates the gold value of an item based on multiple factors including base cost, quality, durability, sockets, prefixes/suffixes, set/unique status, and difficulty level modifiers.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input - return 0x7FFFFFFF (max int) if pUnit or in_EAX is NULL or unit type != 4 (item)
2. Early exit checks: Check if item is identified (mode 3), check indestructible flag (0x20000)
3. Get item stat 0x46 (item level) and stat 0x57 (reduced value percent, capped at 99)
4. Mode 2 (repair cost): Get base repair value from item data table offset 0xD4
5. Calculate base value from item record at offset 0xE0
6. Apply quality modifiers based on item quality type (1-9): normal, magic, rare, set, unique, crafted
7. Apply set/unique bonuses using Ordinal_11124 lookup tables at offsets 0x88/0x8C
8. Apply quantity divisor for stackable items
9. Apply socketed gem/rune bonuses via FUN_6fd912e0 and FUN_6fd910b0
10. Apply difficulty scaling via Ordinal_10301 difficulty table
11. Apply item condition modifiers (durability checks via stat 0x48 vs max durability)
12. Clamp final value and apply reduced value percent discount if applicable

Parameters:
  pUnit (int*): Pointer to item unit structure (unit type must be 4)
  nItemSlot (int): Inventory slot index for item
  pInventory (int*): Pointer to inventory structure
  nDifficulty (int): Game difficulty level (0=Normal, 1=Nightmare, 2=Hell)
  nValueMode (int): Value calculation mode (1=sell, 2=repair, 3=buy)
  IMPLICIT in_EAX: Source unit (player/NPC) for transaction context

Returns:
  int: Calculated gold value of item
       0x7FFFFFFF if invalid input
       0 if unidentified item in buy mode
       1 if indestructible
       Minimum 1 for valid calculations

Special Cases:
  - Indestructible items (flag 0x20000) return value of 1
  - Unidentified items in mode 3 (buy) return 0
  - Items with reduced value stat (0x57) get percentage discount
  - Stackable items divide by quantity
  - Quality types affect switch at offset 0x6fd95802

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x46: Item level stat ID
  0x48: Current durability stat ID
  0x57: Reduced value percent stat ID
  0xFC: Indestructible flag stat
  0xFD: Cannot be repaired stat
  0xE0: Base value offset in item record
  0xD4: Repair cost offset in item record
  0xCC/0xD0: Min/max level range offsets
  0x10000: Threshold for high value calculations
  0x3FF (1023): Fixed point rounding mask (10-bit)

functions.name: ProcessRoomTileAdjustments
functions.signature: void ProcessRoomTileAdjustments(int nIsFirstColumn, int nIsFirstRow, int * pnPrimaryTileData, int * pnSecondaryTileData, int nDefaultTileValue)
functions.comment:
Processes room tile adjustments for DRLG level generation.

Iterates over a 2D grid of tiles and accumulates adjustment values based on tile
flags into the room's adjustment structure. This function is called during room
tile processing to calculate visual adjustments for floor, wall, and roof tiles.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate effective row/column counts based on boundary flags
2. For each tile in the grid:
   a. Read tile flags from primary tile data array
   b. Check if tile has adjustment flags (0x8000003 mask)
   c. Optionally read tile value from secondary data or use default
   d. Extract tile type (bits 20-25) and subtype (bits 8-15)
   e. Call D2CMP::Ordinal_10066 to get tile info into buffer
   f. Call D2CMP::Ordinal_10027 to validate tile (check bit 8)
   g. Based on flag bits, add adjustment to appropriate offset:
      - Bit 1: offset +0x18 (floor adjustments)
      - Bit 2: offset +0x20 (wall adjustments)
      - Neither: offset +0x28 (roof adjustments)
   h. Set dirty flag (0x8000000) at context+0xE0

Parameters:
  nIsFirstColumn (ECX): 1 if processing first column, adds +1 to column count
  nIsFirstRow (EDX): 1 if processing first row, adds +1 to row count
  pnPrimaryTileData: Pointer to primary tile data array structure
  pnSecondaryTileData: Optional pointer to secondary tile data (can be NULL)
  nDefaultTileValue: Default tile value when secondary data is NULL

IMPLICIT Parameters:
  in_EAX: Column boundary flag from caller (inverted - 0 adds +1 to count)
  unaff_EDI: Room context structure pointer

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x8000003 - Tile adjustment flag mask (bits 0, 1, 25)
  0x8000000 - Room dirty/modified flag
  0x28 - Tile info buffer size for D2CMP call
  0x3F - Mask for 6-bit tile type extraction

Structure Offsets (Room Context at EDI):
  +0x28: Column count for tile iteration
  +0x2C: Row count for tile iteration
  +0x3C: Tile set data pointer (passed to D2CMP)
  +0xE0: Room flags (dirty flag set here)
  +0xE4: Pointer to adjustment accumulator structure

Adjustment Structure Offsets (at +0xE4):
  +0x18: Floor tile adjustments
  +0x20: Wall tile adjustments
  +0x28: Roof tile adjustments

functions.comment:
Builds a COF (Composite Object File) animation file path for game entities.

Algorithm:
1. Determine entity type from dwEntityType (0=Character, 1=Monster, 2=Object)
2. Validate index bounds for the entity type's data table
3. Extract 3-letter animation token from data table offset 0x10 (mode) or 0x20 (weapon)
4. For special weapon classes (0 or 0xC/0x11), use default "hth " (hand-to-hand)
5. Call Ordinal_11120 to resolve animation token from mode/weapon tables
6. Search override tables (g_adwCrtDataBlock_*) for matching weapon class replacements
7. For Character type 0xB, validate token against known values (hs1, ht1, js1, jt1, ss1, st1)
8. Strip space characters (0x20) from each byte of the 3-char tokens
9. Format final path string using wsprintfA:
   - If nUseFullPath=0: "%s%s%s" (just tokens concatenated)
   - If nUseFullPath=1: "DATA\GLOBAL\{TYPE}\{token}\COF\{mode}{weapon}{anim}.COF"

Parameters:
  pnUnitId (int*): Unit identifier, used for animation resolution
  dwModeIndex (dword): Animation mode index in data tables
  dwWeaponClass (dword): Weapon class/type index
  dwEntityType (dword): Entity type: 0=CHAR, 1=MONSTER, 2=OBJECT
  pnOutputFlags (int*): Output flags from Ordinal_11120
  lpszOutputPath (LPSTR): Output buffer for formatted file path
  pbAnimToken (byte*): 4-byte output buffer for animation token (3 chars + null/space)
  nUseFullPath (int): 0=token only, 1=full DATA\GLOBAL path
  dwSecondaryClass (dword): Secondary animation class for Characters

Returns:
  void - Results written to lpszOutputPath and pbAnimToken

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x68 0x74 0x68 0x20 = "hth " - Default hand-to-hand animation token
  0x20736831 = "1hs " - One-handed swing
  0x20746831 = "1ht " - One-handed thrust
  0x20736a31 = "1js " - Javelin swing
  0x20746a31 = "1jt " - Javelin thrust
  0x20737331 = "1ss " - Staff swing
  0x20747331 = "1st " - Staff thrust
  0x1a8 = Monster record size (424 bytes)
  0x34 = Standard data record size (52 bytes)

Data Table Offsets:
  +0x10: Mode animation token (3 chars)
  +0x20: Weapon animation token (3 chars)
  +0xa78: Monster stats table pointer
  +0xa80: Monster stats table count

functions.name: FindOptimalPath
functions.signature: int FindOptimalPath(uint * pTargetCoords, uint dwStartCoord, uint * pPathBuffer, int * pnPathIndex, int * pnPathLength, int nMaxSteps, int nSearchDirection)
functions.comment:
Finds an optimal path between two coordinates using dual-path search algorithm.

This function implements a bidirectional pathfinding algorithm that explores from both
the current position and an alternate starting point, selecting the shorter path.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize two path state structures (primary at -0x350, alternate at -0x698)
2. Set neighbor lookup table pointers for each path state
3. Calculate initial direction index from packed coordinate deltas using g_adwDirectionLookupTable
4. Main loop: Check if current tile is walkable via FUN_6fd9c1e0 collision test
5. Calculate directional distance based on nSearchDirection (0=N, 1=E, 2=S, 3=W)
6. If path connects to existing path in buffer, merge via FUN_6fd9bf10 and return
7. Track visited coordinates and detect path intersection between primary and alternate
8. When both paths complete, compare squared distances to target position
9. Select shorter path and copy coordinates to output buffer
10. Update path indices and return step count

Parameters:
  pTargetCoords - Pointer to target coordinate pair (uint[2])
                  [0] = Current packed X/Y coord, [1] = Destination packed X/Y
  dwStartCoord - Starting coordinate (X in bits 0-15, Y in bits 16-31)
  pPathBuffer - Output buffer for path waypoint coordinates (uint array)
  pnPathIndex - Pointer to current write index in path buffer (in/out)
  pnPathLength - Pointer to total path length (in/out)
  nMaxSteps - Maximum steps allowed (>80 triggers early exit with 0)
  nSearchDirection - Direction bias: 0=North, 1=East, 2=South, 3=West

Returns:
  >0: Number of path steps added on success
  0: Path not found, target already reached, or paths intersected

Magic Numbers:
  0x1bb (443) - Error code for exceeding max steps (triggers abort)
  0x50 (80) - Max steps threshold for early return
  0xC8 (200) - Path buffer size in DWORDs

Global Data:
  g_adwDirectionLookupTable (0x6fde2698) - Direction index lookup table
  g_abPrimaryNeighborOffsetX (0x6fde2648) - Primary X neighbor offsets
  g_abPrimaryNeighborOffsetY (0x6fde25c8) - Primary Y neighbor offsets
  g_abAltNeighborOffsetX (0x6fde2608) - Alternate X neighbor offsets
  g_abAltNeighborOffsetY (0x6fde2588) - Alternate Y neighbor offsets

functions.name: SetOverlayPositionAndLayer
functions.signature: int SetOverlayPositionAndLayer(int nUnused, void * pContext, int nFlags, int * pnOverlayData, int nParam5, short nOverlayIndex, int nParam7, int nParam8, int nParam9, uint dwParam10)
functions.comment:
Sets an overlay's position and layer in the rendering system.
This function validates the overlay index and data, clamps coordinates,
then updates the overlay context with a packed position value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pnOverlayData is non-null; return 0 if null.
2. Validate nOverlayIndex is in valid range [0, overlay table count).
3. Validate overlay table entry exists at index * 0x144.
4. Extract layer, X, Y from pnOverlayData structure (offsets [1], [2], [3]).
5. Apply 256 (0x100) offset to X and Y coordinates.
6. Clamp layer to range [0, 3].
7. Clamp X to range [0, 1023 (0x3ff)].
8. Clamp Y to range [0, 1023 (0x3ff)].
9. Get or create overlay context via FUN_6fda3ff0.
10. If context valid, call Ordinal_10463 to set packed position value.
11. Return clamped Y coordinate on success, 0 on failure.

Parameters:
- nUnused (ECX): Unused first fastcall register parameter.
- pContext (EDX): Overlay context pointer passed to FUN_6fda3ff0.
- nFlags: Reserved flags (unused in this function).
- pnOverlayData: Pointer to int array containing overlay data:
  [1]: Layer index (0-3)
  [2]: X coordinate (will be offset by 256)
  [3]: Y coordinate (will be offset by 256)
- nParam5: Reserved parameter (unused).
- nOverlayIndex: Index into overlay table (stride 0x144 = 324 bytes).
- nParam7: Reserved parameter (unused).
- nParam8: Reserved parameter (unused).
- nParam9: Parameter passed to FUN_6fda3ff0.
- dwParam10: Parameter passed to FUN_6fda3ff0.

Returns:
- Clamped Y coordinate (0-1023) on success.
- 0 on failure (null data, invalid index, or context allocation failure).

Magic Numbers:
- 0x100 (256): Coordinate offset applied to X and Y.
- 0x3ff (1023): Maximum coordinate value after clamping.
- 0x144 (324): Overlay table entry stride in bytes.
- 0x400 (1024): Y coordinate multiplier in packed value.
- 0xbcc, 0xbd4: sgptDataTables offsets for overlay table ptr and count.

functions.signature: int WriteTileDataToMap(uint dwUnused, void * pTileData, uint dwParam3, int * pnMapBounds, uint dwUnused2, uint dwTileValue, int nLookupKey, uint dwHashParam)
functions.comment:
Writes tile data to the map at validated coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Validate coordinate bounds (pnMapBounds[2] must be <= pnMapBounds[3])
2. Extract layer index from pnMapBounds[1] and adjust X/Y by adding 0x100
3. Acquire tile node via FUN_6fda3ff0 using lookup key and hash parameter
4. Validate layer index is in range [0, 3]
5. Validate adjusted X coordinate is in range [0, 0x3FF] (0-1023)
6. Validate adjusted Y coordinate is in range [0, 0x3FF] (0-1023)
7. Compute tile index: layer + (Y * 1024 + X) * 4
8. Call Ordinal_10463 (D2Common.StoreTileData) to write tile value at computed index

Parameters:
  dwUnused (ECX) - uint: Unused parameter
  pTileData (EDX) - void*: Pointer to tile data context (passed to FUN_6fda3ff0)
  dwParam3 - uint: Unused stack parameter
  pnMapBounds - int*: Pointer to map bounds array:
    [0]: Unknown
    [1]: Layer index (0-3)
    [2]: Minimum coordinate
    [3]: Maximum coordinate
  dwUnused2 - uint: Tile value to write (passed to Ordinal_10463)
  dwTileValue - uint: Additional tile parameter
  nLookupKey - int: Lookup key for tile node acquisition
  dwHashParam - uint: Hash parameter for tile node lookup

Returns:
  1 - Success, tile data written
  Does not return on validation failure (calls CleanupAndAbort)

Ordinal Calls:
  Ordinal_10463 = D2Common.StoreTileData - Writes tile value at computed map index

Error Codes (line numbers passed to CleanupAndAbort):
  0x444 (1092) - Coordinate bounds invalid (min > max)
  0x44A (1098) - Failed to acquire tile node (null pointer)
  0x44C (1100) - Layer index out of range (not 0-3)
  0x44D (1101) - Adjusted X coordinate out of range (not 0-1023)
  0x44E (1102) - Adjusted Y coordinate out of range (not 0-1023)

Magic Numbers:
  0x100 (256) - Coordinate offset adjustment
  0x400 (1024) - Map dimension (width/height)
  0x3FF (1023) - Maximum valid coordinate value
  0x3 - Maximum layer index

functions.name: CalculateAndApplySkillEffect
functions.signature: int CalculateAndApplySkillEffect(int nUnused, void * pContext, int * pUnit, int nSkillDataAddr, int nBaseValue, int nModifier, int nEffectType, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Calculates and applies a skill effect value based on skill level and unit stats.

Algorithm:
  1. Validate nSkillDataAddr is non-null, return 0 if null
  2. Extract skill ID from nSkillDataAddr+4, validate against skill table bounds (0 to sgptDataTables+0xba0)
  3. Calculate skill record address: sgptDataTables+0xb98 + (skillId * 0x23c), return 0 if null
  4. Read modifier from nSkillDataAddr+0xc to determine effect level calculation method:
     - If modifier == 0: level = ((unitLevel - skillReqLevel) / 4) + 1, clamped by max skill level
     - If modifier < 0: level = (unitLevel - skillReqLevel) / scaleFactor
     - Otherwise: use modifier directly as the effect level
  5. Read magnitude from nSkillDataAddr+8:
     - If 0: default to 5
     - If negative: scale by -(value) + (level * -value / 8)
     - Clamp final value to range [1, 255]
  6. Get random value from unit seed via RNG (Ordinal_10691 + FUN_6fd51050)
  7. Allocate/get skill result structure via FUN_6fda3ff0(pContext, nEffectType, dwFlags)
  8. Apply effect via Ordinal_10463: packedValue = (randomBase & 0xFF) | (finalMagnitude << 8)

Parameters:
  nUnused (ECX): Unused register parameter, preserved for __fastcall convention
  pContext (EDX): Context pointer passed to skill result allocation function
  pUnit: Pointer to unit structure providing level stat and random seed
  nSkillDataAddr: Address of skill data structure: +4=skillId, +8=magnitude, +0xC=modifier
  nBaseValue: Base stat value passed to Ordinal_10463
  nModifier: Modifier passed to Ordinal_10463 (shifted by skill bit count)
  nEffectType: Effect type identifier for skill allocation
  dwFlags: Flags for skill allocation and type identification

Returns:
  1 on success (effect was calculated and applied)
  0 if nSkillDataAddr is null or skill ID is invalid/out of bounds

Magic Numbers:
  0x23c (572): Size of skill data record in sgptDataTables skill array
  0xb98: Offset to skill data array pointer in sgptDataTables
  0xba0: Offset to skill count in sgptDataTables
  0x174: Offset to skill level requirement within skill record
  99: Maximum character level used for scaling calculations
  0xff (255): Maximum allowed effect magnitude value
  0x100 (256): Shift factor for packing magnitude into result

functions.name: ApplyItemStatModifiers
functions.signature: int ApplyItemStatModifiers(uint dwParam1, void * pContext, int * pUnit, int nItemData, int nStatBase, uint dwParam6, uint dwParam7, int nModifierValue, int nParam9, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Applies item stat modifiers (life steal, mana steal, physical damage) to a unit based on item properties.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pItemData is non-null
2. Validate pUnit is non-null and is type 4 (item)
3. Get item record structure via FUN_6fda29b0
4. If nModifierValue is 0, calculate base modifier from item data offset 0x8
5. Check flag 0x2D and apply life steal modifier (stat 0x16) from offset 0xFF
6. Check flag 0x2D and apply mana steal modifier (stat 0x18) from offset 0x103
7. Check flag 0x2D and stackable flag, apply physical damage modifier (stat 0xA0) from offset 0x101
8. Return final modifier value

Parameters:
  dwParam1 - uint: IMPLICIT via ECX, unused
  pContext - void*: IMPLICIT via EDX, context passed to stat application
  pUnit - int*: Pointer to unit structure, must be type 4 (item)
  pItemData - int: Pointer to item data, contains offsets 0x8 and 0xC
  nStatBase - int: Base stat mode (0 = set, non-zero = add)
  dwParam6 - uint: Unused parameter
  dwParam7 - uint: Unused parameter
  nModifierValue - int: Base modifier value, calculated if 0
  nParam9 - int: Passed to FUN_6fda45b0
  dwFlags - uint: Flags passed to FUN_6fda45b0

Returns:
  int: Final modifier value (nModifierValue), or 0 on validation failure

Magic Numbers:
  0x2D (45) - Item flag checked via Ordinal_10731
  0x16 (22) - Life Steal stat ID
  0x18 (24) - Mana Steal stat ID
  0xA0 (160) - Physical Damage modifier stat ID
  0xFF (255) - Item record offset for life steal modifier byte
  0x101 (257) - Item record offset for physical damage modifier byte
  0x103 (259) - Item record offset for mana steal modifier byte

Called By:
  FUN_6fda6130, FUN_6fda61d0, FUN_6fda62b0

Calls:
  FUN_6fda29b0 - Gets item record from unit
  FUN_6fda3520 - Calculates base modifier value
  FUN_6fda45b0 - Applies stat modifier to unit
  Ordinal_10731 - Checks item flag (D2Common)
  Ordinal_10193 - Checks if item is stackable (D2Common)

functions.name: ApplyItemRegenStats
functions.signature: int ApplyItemRegenStats(int nStatList, UnitAny * pOwnerUnit, int * pItem, int nItemData, int nApplyMode, int nStatId, int nUnused, int nBaseValue, int nStatParam, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Applies life, mana, and stamina regeneration stats from an item to the owner unit.

Algorithm:
1. Validate nItemData is not null, return 0 if invalid
2. Validate pItem is a valid item unit (type == 4), return 0 if invalid
3. Get item record via FUN_6fda29b0 (GetItemRecord), return 0 if not found
4. If nBaseValue is 0, calculate from item data via FUN_6fda3520 (GetStatValue)
5. Check stat 0x2d (45) via Ordinal_10731 (UNITS_GetStatValue):
   - If not present OR life regen modifier set OR mana regen not set:
     Apply stat 0x15 (21 - hpregen) with adjusted value
6. Check stat 0x2d again:
   - If not present OR mana regen modifier set OR life regen not set:
     Apply stat 0x17 (23 - manaregen) with adjusted value
7. Check stat 0x2d again:
   - If present AND Ordinal_10193 (ITEMS_CheckNormalType) returns 0:
     Skip stamina regen, return base value early
8. Apply stat 0x9f (159 - staminaregen) with adjusted value
9. Return nBaseValue

Parameters:
  nStatList (ECX): Stat list pointer (implicit, unused in function body)
  pOwnerUnit (EDX): UnitAny pointer - Owner unit receiving the stats
  pItem: Item unit pointer, must be type 4 (item)
  nItemData: Item data structure pointer with field at offset +8
  nApplyMode: 0 = set stat, non-zero = add stat
  nStatId: Stat ID (unused, hardcoded 0x15/0x17/0x9f used)
  nUnused: Unused parameter
  nBaseValue: Base regeneration value, calculated if 0
  nStatParam: Stat parameter passed to apply function
  dwFlags: Flags passed to apply function

Returns:
  nBaseValue on success (may be calculated if input was 0)
  0 on failure (null pointers, invalid item type, no record)

Item Record Offsets:
  0xFE (254): Life regen modifier byte
  0x100 (256): Stamina regen modifier byte
  0x102 (258): Mana regen modifier byte

Stat IDs:
  0x15 (21): hpregen - Life regeneration
  0x17 (23): manaregen - Mana regeneration
  0x2d (45): Item stat check (quality/type flag)
  0x9f (159): staminaregen - Stamina regeneration

Ordinal Calls:
  Ordinal_10731 = UNITS_GetStatValue - Returns stat value for unit
  Ordinal_10193 = ITEMS_CheckNormalType - Returns 1 if item is normal type

Decompiler Variables (SSA - regenerated each decompile):
  bVar1: Regeneration modifier byte from item record
  uVar2: Result of Ordinal_10193 (normal item check)
  iVar3: Item record pointer from FUN_6fda29b0
  uVar4: Result of Ordinal_10731 stat check
  iVar5: Adjusted regeneration value after modifier calculation
  extraout_var: Extended return value (upper 3 bytes of EAX)

functions.name: ApplyBidirectionalStatModifiers
functions.signature: int ApplyBidirectionalStatModifiers(int nStatBase, UnitAny * pUnit, int * pnOutItemData, int nStatParam1, int nStatParam2, int nStatParam3, int nStatParam4, int nModifierBase, int nModifierMax, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Applies bidirectional stat modifiers to an item unit, handling min/max damage pairs.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if nStatParam1 (unit pointer from stack) is NULL, returns 0
2. If nModifierMax is NULL, calculate modifier using FUN_6fda3520 from stat base
3. Check if item type is 4 (weapon/equipment); if not type 4, report error 0x61C
4. Call Ordinal_10600 (GetUnitFromId) to get item data pointer, validate non-NULL
5. Lookup item in g_pItemDataBuffer using BinarySearchTable with item ID at offset 0x80
6. Calculate item record address: index * 0x1A8 + g_pItemRecordBaseArray
7. Apply damage stats via Ordinal_10043 (SetUnitStat) from item record offsets
8. Check Ordinal_10193 (CheckItemValid) for mastery stat application
9. Calculate random modifier using FUN_6fd51150 with base 100
10. If modifier check passes, call ApplyItemStatModifiers recursively
11. Otherwise call FUN_6fda45b0 twice with stat IDs 0x12 and 0x11

Parameters:
nStatBase (ECX) - Stat base structure pointer with arrays at +0x8 and +0xC
pUnit (EDX) - UnitAny pointer receiving stat modifications
pnOutItemData - Output pointer for calculated item data
nStatParam1 - Primary unit context parameter
nStatParam2 - Secondary modifier parameter
nStatParam3 - Tertiary stat parameter
nStatParam4 - Quaternary stat parameter
nModifierBase - Base modifier value (0 = calculate from item)
nModifierMax - Maximum modifier cap
dwFlags - Stat application behavior flags

Returns:
1 - Stats successfully applied; 0 - NULL pointer or validation failure
nModifierMax - Returned on recursive ApplyItemStatModifiers path

Magic Numbers:
0x1A8 - Item record structure size
0x80 - Item ID offset in data structure
0xFE-0x103 - Damage stat byte offsets
0x2D - Damage validation stat ID
0x11/0x12 - Secondary damage stat IDs
0x15-0x18 - Primary damage min/max stat IDs
0x9F/0xA0 - Mastery damage stat IDs

Ordinal References:
Ordinal_10043 - SetUnitStat
Ordinal_10193 - CheckItemValid
Ordinal_10600 - GetUnitFromId
Ordinal_10731 - GetItemStat

functions.name: LoadBeltsTxtData
functions.comment:
Loads and parses the belts.txt data table into memory.

Algorithm:
1. Allocates 0x52c bytes on stack for 66 FormatDescriptor entries (66 * 20 = 0x528 bytes)
2. Initializes field descriptor array with column definitions for belt properties:
   - numboxes, box1left, box1right, box2left, box2right, etc. (inventory slot positions)
   - Each descriptor contains: field name pointer, field type (2=short, 4=dword, 8=string), flags, offset
3. Calls DATATBLS_LoadTextFile with "belts" filename and descriptor array
4. Stores returned record pointer in g_pBeltsTxtRecords global
5. Validates record count equals 7 (number of belt types), aborts on mismatch

Parameters:
- dwUnused (ECX): IMPLICIT - Unused parameter, passed through to DATATBLS_LoadTextFile
- pMemPool (EDX): IMPLICIT - Memory pool pointer for allocation

Returns:
- void (result stored in g_pBeltsTxtRecords global at 0x6fdefe08)

Error Handling:

functions.name: InitRoomCollisionData
functions.comment:
Initializes collision data for a room by allocating and populating a collision grid structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pRoom is not NULL (early exit if NULL)
2. Call Ordinal_10991 to retrieve room dimension data (8 DWORDs)
3. Calculate collision grid size: width * height * 2 bytes
4. Allocate memory for collision data structure via AllocPoolMemoryTracked
5. Copy the 8 DWORD room dimension info to allocated structure
6. Store collision data pointer at pRoom+0x60
7. Set grid pointer at offset 0x20 (pointing to grid data at offset 0x24)
8. Zero-initialize the collision grid memory
9. Iterate through unit array at pRoom+0x34 (count at pRoom+0x7c)
10. For each unit, process three collision sets via FUN_6fdaa220:
    - Primary collision data (unit+0x58 fields at offsets 0x8, 0xC)
    - Secondary collision data (unit+0x58 fields at offsets 0x0, 0x4)
    - Tertiary collision data (unit+0x58 fields at offsets 0x10, 0x14)

Parameters:
  dwUnused - Unused parameter (always ignored)
  pRoom - Pointer to Room structure to initialize collision for

Returns:
  void - No return value

Error Handling:
  Calls CleanupAndAbort with error codes if unit pointer is NULL:
  - 0x2C5 (709): NULL unit in first access
  - 0xB1 (177): NULL unit in second access
  - 0xBE (190): NULL unit in third access

Structure Layout (Collision Data at pRoom+0x60):
  Offset  Size  Field             Description
  0x00    0x20  anRoomDimensions  8 DWORDs of room dimension data
  0x20    0x04  pGridData         Pointer to collision grid (points to 0x24)
  0x24    var   abGridData        Collision grid bytes (width*height*2)

Magic Numbers:
  0x185 - Source line number for AllocPoolMemoryTracked
  0x60 - Room offset for collision data pointer
  0x7c - Room offset for unit count
  0x34 - Room offset for unit list array
  0x58 - Unit offset for collision info structure

functions.name: FindNearestValidPosition
functions.signature: void * FindNearestValidPosition(dword dwUnknownParam, int * pnCoordXY, int * pnSecondaryCoordXY, dword dwParam4, dword dwFlags, dword dwParam6, int nAllowFallback, int nMaxSearchRadius, int nSearchStep)
functions.comment:
Finds the nearest valid position to the initial coordinates using a spiral search pattern.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input coordinates pointer (abort if null)
2. Extract initial X,Y from pnCoordXY
3. If secondary coordinates provided, allocate Room and set bounds via Ordinal_10637/SetRoomMinBounds
4. Try initial position first using FUN_6fd512b0 allocation and Ordinal_10701 validation
5. If initial position valid, optionally validate against room using Ordinal_10867
6. If initial position fails, perform spiral search expanding outward:
   a. Search pattern alternates between two phases per ring
   b. First phase scans rows from top to bottom of current ring
   c. Second phase scans columns from left to right of current ring
   d. Track best position using Manhattan distance from origin
7. Continue until valid position found or radius exceeds nMaxSearchRadius
8. Free Room if allocated; return best position or null

Parameters:
  dwUnknownParam - Unused parameter (reserved)
  pnCoordXY - Pointer to [X,Y] integer pair (input: initial coords, output: best valid coords)
  pnSecondaryCoordXY - Optional pointer to [X,Y] secondary bounds for room constraint
  dwParam4 - Validation parameter passed to Ordinal_10701
  dwFlags - Flags passed to Ordinal_10701 for position validation
  dwParam6 - Parameter passed to Ordinal_10867 for room validation
  nAllowFallback - If non-zero, return last allocation even if no valid position found
  nMaxSearchRadius - Maximum search distance from origin before giving up
  nSearchStep - Step size for expanding search ring (typically 1)

Returns:
  void* - Allocated position object on success, NULL if no valid position and nAllowFallback is 0

Magic Numbers:
  0x726 (1830) - Line number for null pnCoordXY abort
  0x730 (1840) - Line number for null Room allocation abort
  -1 - Sentinel value for nBestDistance (no valid position found yet)

Error Handling:
  Aborts via CleanupAndAbort/ReportError if pnCoordXY is null or Room allocation fails

functions.name: ExpandPathNode
functions.signature: int * ExpandPathNode(dword * pPathContext, int nMaxCost, dword * pDrlgRoom, int * pTargetCoord)
functions.comment:
Expands pathfinding nodes using A* heuristic search for DRLG vertex path generation.

Algorithm:
1. Start with current node from path context at pPathContext[0]
2. Check if current node position matches target coordinates - return node if found
3. Calculate next position using direction delta tables (g_abDirDeltaX, g_abDirDeltaY)
4. Validate next tile is walkable via FUN_6fdab120 collision check
5. Compute movement cost: 2 for cardinal directions, 3 for diagonal
6. Calculate Manhattan-style heuristic: min(deltaX,deltaY) + max(deltaX,deltaY)*2
7. If total cost (pathCost + heuristic) is within nMaxCost threshold:
   a. Allocate new node from pool (max 900 nodes at offset 0x2329)
   b. Initialize node fields: totalCost, heuristic, pathCost, position
   c. Link parent node via offset 0x20, update direction via rotation table
8. If cost exceeds threshold, advance to next open node via FUN_6fdab040
9. Continue loop until target found or all nodes exhausted

Parameters:
pPathContext - Pointer to path context structure containing node pool
nMaxCost - Maximum allowed total path cost for pruning branches
pDrlgRoom - DRLG room pointer passed to collision validation
pTargetCoord - Pointer to target X,Y coordinates (two consecutive ints)

Returns:
Pointer to path node that reached target coordinates
NULL if node pool exhausted (900 max) or no valid path exists

Path Node Structure (40 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field
0x00    4     nTotalCost (f = g + h)
0x04    4     nHeuristic (h estimate)
0x08    4     nPathCost (g from start)
0x0C    4     nPosX
0x10    4     nPosY
0x14    4     dwFlags
0x18    4     pDirTable
0x1C    1     bDirection (0-3)
0x20    4     pParent
0x24    4     pChild

Magic Numbers:
900 (0x384) - Maximum node pool size
0x2329 - Node count offset in path context
2 - Cardinal movement cost
3 - Diagonal movement cost

functions.name: BuildDrlgVertexPath
functions.comment:
Builds a vertex path between start and end points in a DRLG room.

Calculates tile coordinates from room offset data, determines if direct connection
is possible (Manhattan distance <= 2), otherwise uses iterative pathfinding with
increasing cost thresholds until a valid path is found or iteration limit reached.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate start tile coordinates from room data at offset +0xF8/+0xFC
2. Calculate end tile coordinates from room data at offset +0x170/+0x174
3. Convert world coordinates to tile coordinates (divide by 8)
4. Check Manhattan distance between start and end points
5. If distance <= 2: Allocate direct vertex nodes for start and end
6. If distance > 2: Use iterative A* pathfinding via FUN_6fdab1d0
   a. Calculate initial direction from GetPrimaryDir8FromDeltas
   b. Loop with increasing path cost threshold (+5 per iteration)
   c. Allocate vertex nodes for each path segment found
7. Return 1 on success, 0 on failure

Parameters:
pRoom - Pointer to DRLG room structure containing coordinate offsets
IMPLICIT EBX - Vertex index within room (used for array indexing at +0x68)

Returns:
1 - Path successfully built and vertices allocated
0 - Failed to find path within 900 iterations or cost threshold exceeded

Structure Layout (Vertex Node - 0x14 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field       Description
0x00    4     nTileX      Tile X coordinate
0x04    4     nTileY      Tile Y coordinate
0x08    1     bFlags      Direction/state flags
0x10    4     pNext       Pointer to next vertex node

Magic Numbers:
0x8 - Tile size divisor (world coords to tiles)
0x14 (20) - Size of vertex node allocation
0x13 (19) - Pool ID for vertex memory allocation
0x384 (900) - Maximum iteration count
0x23 (35) - Initial path cost padding
0x5 - Cost increment per iteration
0x8D08 (36104) - Stack frame size for path buffer array (900 nodes * 40 bytes)

Phantom Variables:
uStack_8c80..uStack_8cdc are decompiler-generated temporaries for accessing
elements within the large anPathNodes[900] stack array and cannot be renamed.

Error Handling:
Returns 0 if pathfinding exceeds 900 iterations without finding valid path

functions.name: GenerateRandomCharacterStats
functions.signature: undefined4 GenerateRandomCharacterStats(int nSeed, int * pnCharStats, byte bDifficulty)
functions.comment:
Generates randomized character statistics based on class and difficulty.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters (seed != 0, stats ptr != NULL, difficulty < 3)
2. Get class index from stats[0] and validate range [0-3]
3. Initialize PRNG state with seed and magic constant 0x29A
4. Clear special flag at offset 0x38
5. Set base Y-stat (offset 0x34) and X-stat (offset 0x20) from class tables
6. Roll Table 1: Generate random index, lookup stats for offset 0x04/0x18, accumulate X/Y mods
7. Roll Table 2: Generate random index, lookup stats for offset 0x08/0x1C, accumulate X/Y mods
8. Roll Table 3: Generate random index with stride 0x18
   - If class < 3: set offset 0x0C to table value, offset 0x14 to 0
   - If class >= 3: set offset 0x0C to 0, offset 0x14 to table value
   - Set offsets 0x24 and 0x28 from table
   - If table flag is 0, set special flag at offset 0x38 to 1
   - Accumulate X/Y mods
9. Roll Table 4: Generate random index with stride 0x14
   - Set offset 0x2C (stat11) and 0x30 (stat12) from table
   - If stat11 is 9-11, set offset 0x10 to 1 (special ability flag)
   - Accumulate X/Y mods
10. Apply difficulty modifiers if bDifficulty != 0:
    - Add offsets to stats at 0x18, 0x1C, 0x20
    - Multiply stats at 0x24, 0x28, 0x34
    - Add offset to stat at 0x30

Parameters:
  nSeed (ECX): Random seed for PRNG initialization
  pnCharStats (EDX): Pointer to character stats structure (60 bytes, 15 dwords)
  bDifficulty (Stack+4): Difficulty level (0=Normal, 1=Hard, 2=Expert)

Returns:
  1 (TRUE): Success - stats were generated
  0 (FALSE): Failure - invalid parameters or class index out of range

Structure Layout (pnCharStats):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x00    4     nClassIndex     Character class (0-3)
  0x04    4     nStat1          Table 1 primary stat
  0x08    4     nStat2          Table 2 primary stat
  0x0C    4     nStat3A         Table 3 stat (class 0-2)
  0x10    4     nSpecialFlag    1 if stat11 is 9-11
  0x14    4     nStat3B         Table 3 stat (class 3)
  0x18    4     nStat6          Table 1 secondary stat
  0x1C    4     nStat7          Table 2 secondary stat
  0x20    4     nStatX          Accumulated X-stat
  0x24    4     nStat9          Table 3 stat, difficulty multiplied
  0x28    4     nStat10         Table 3 stat, difficulty multiplied
  0x2C    4     nStat11         Table 4 primary (determines special flag)
  0x30    4     nStat12         Table 4 secondary, difficulty modified
  0x34    4     nStatY          Accumulated Y-stat
  0x38    2     wSpecialFlag2   Set to 1 if Table 3 flag is 0

Magic Numbers:
  0x29A: PRNG magic constant (666 decimal)
  0x10: Table 1/2 record stride (16 bytes per entry)
  0x18: Table 3 record stride (24 bytes per entry)
  0x14: Table 4 record stride (20 bytes per entry)
  0x1C: Difficulty modifier stride (28 bytes per level)

functions.name: LoadOverlayTextFile
functions.comment:
Loads and parses the overlay.txt data table from the MPQ archive.

Algorithm:
1. Initializes a FormatDescriptor array (26 entries) on the stack defining all overlay.txt columns
2. Registers the source file (OverlayTbls.cpp) with FOG for debugging/logging
3. Calls DATATBLS_LoadTextFile to parse overlay.txt using the format descriptor
4. Stores the result in g_pOverlayData global and record count in g_nOverlayRecordCount

Parameters:
  pMemPool (void*) - Memory pool for allocation during table loading

Returns:
  void - Results stored in global variables g_pOverlayData and g_nOverlayRecordCount

Overlay.txt Fields (26 columns):
  Offset 0x00: type - Table name string "overlay"
  Offset 0x40: Filename - DC6 animation filename (string, 64 bytes max)
  Offset 0x42: version - Version number (short)
  Offset 0x44: Frames - Animation frame count (short)
  Offset 0x48: PreDraw - Pre-draw flag (bool)
  Offset 0x4C: 1ofN - Random selection (short)
  Offset 0x50: Dir - Directional flag (bool)
  Offset 0x51: Open - Open overlay flag (bool)
  Offset 0x52: Beta - Beta content flag (bool)
  Offset 0x54: Xoffset - X display offset (short)
  Offset 0x58: Yoffset - Y display offset (short)
  Offset 0x5C: Height1 - Height layer 1 (short)
  Offset 0x60: Height2 - Height layer 2 (short)
  Offset 0x64: Height3 - Height layer 3 (short)
  Offset 0x68: Height4 - Height layer 4 (short)
  Offset 0x6C: AnimRate - Animation rate (short)
  Offset 0x70: InitRadius - Initial light radius (short)
  Offset 0x74: Radius - Light radius (short)
  Offset 0x78: LoopWaitTime - Loop wait delay (short)
  Offset 0x7C: Trans - Transparency mode (bool)
  Offset 0x7D: Red - RGB red component (byte)
  Offset 0x7E: Green - RGB green component (byte)
  Offset 0x7F: Blue - RGB blue component (byte)
  Offset 0x80: NumDirections - Direction count (bool)

functions.name: CopyStringWithSpacePadding
functions.comment:
Copies up to 4 characters from source string to destination buffer, padding with spaces.

This function implements a fixed-width 4-character string copy commonly used in game
data structures for compact string storage. It reads characters from the source string
until either a null terminator is found or all 4 characters are copied, filling any
remaining destination bytes with space characters (0x20).

Algorithm:
1. Load first character from source string
2. If null terminator found, fill all 4 destination bytes with spaces and return
3. Copy first character to destination byte 0
4. Load second character
5. If null terminator found, fill bytes 1-3 with spaces and return
6. Copy second character to destination byte 1
7. Load third character
8. If null terminator found, fill bytes 2-3 with spaces and return
9. Copy third character to destination byte 2
10. Load fourth character
11. If null terminator found, fill byte 3 with space and return
12. Copy fourth character to destination byte 3
13. Return

Parameters:
  szpSourceString (ECX): Pointer to null-terminated source string
  szpDestBuffer (EAX): Pointer to 4-byte destination buffer for output

Returns:
  void - Destination buffer filled with 4-character string (space-padded)

Special Cases:
  Empty string: All 4 destination bytes filled with spaces (0x20)
  1-3 character string: Characters copied followed by space padding to 4 bytes
  4+ character string: Only first 4 characters copied (no null check on 4th)

0x04    4     dwFieldType       Field type identifier (0x3F=string, 0xF=lookup, etc.)
0x08    4     dwFlags           Parsing flags (0=default, 1=???)
0x0C    4     dwRecordOffset    Byte offset within RuneWord record to store value
0x10    4     pLookupTable      Pointer to lookup table (NULL or g_pItemTypesSortedArray, etc.)

functions.name: LoadItemStatCostTable
functions.comment:
Loads and initializes the ItemStatCost.txt data table from the MPQ archive.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize field descriptor array for CSV parsing with 65 field definitions
2. Call Ordinal_10211 to load and parse ItemStatCost.bin from data files
3. Validate stat count does not exceed 511 (0x1FF) maximum; abort if exceeded
4. Store parsed record count in g_nItemStatCostCount global
5. Configure bit encoding: calculate bit count (6-8 bits) and mask for stat IDs
6. Initialize NextInChain tracking array (0x20 DWORDs set to -1) for each stat
7. Process each stat record to build stat group relationships:
   - Check Op field (1-13) to determine stat operation type
   - For valid ops, link stat to its OpStat target via group array
   - Set damage flags based on stat category (0x8e0=min, 0xb68=max, 0xdf0=length)
   - Apply appropriate bit masks from g_pItemStatCostPropertyMasks
8. Build sorted stat array for priority-based display ordering:
   - Collect stats with DescPriority > 0 into awSortArray
   - Sort using qsort with CompareStatsByDescPriority callback
9. Allocate g_pwSortedStatIds array and copy sorted stat indices

Parameters:
  pMemPool - void* - Memory pool handle for tracked allocation (passed to AllocPoolMemoryTracked)

Returns:
  void - No return value; aborts on critical errors (stat count > 511)

Special Cases:
  - If nStatCount > 511: Calls CleanupAndAbort with error, then ReportError(-1)
  - If nStatIdBitCount <= 0 or > 8: Defaults to 6 bits (64 stats max encoded)

  0x144 = 324 bytes - sizeof(ItemStatCostRecord) structure size
  0x1FF = 511 - Maximum allowed stat count
  0x40 = 64 - Maximum stats per group chain
  0x10 = 16 - Maximum OpStat entries per stat record
  0x8e0, 0xb68, 0xdf0 - Record offsets for min/max/length damage stats

  0x34    2     wDescPriority   ushort      Display priority for sorting
  0x36    1     bHasDesc        byte        Has description flag

  0x52    1     bIsDamage       byte        Damage-related stat
  0x53    1     bOpType         byte        Operation type (1-13)
  0x54    1     bOp             byte        Op code value
  0x55    1     bOpParam        byte        Op parameter
  0x56    2     wOpStat         ushort      Target stat for operation
  0x58    6     OpStatChain[3]  ushort[3]   Chain of related stats

functions.name: LoadQualityItemsData

functions.name: LoadUniqueItemsTxt
functions.comment:
Loads and parses the UniqueItems.txt data table from game binary data files.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize FormatDescriptor array with field definitions for 45+ columns
2. Call Ordinal_10211 to allocate memory for table data (line 0x37a)
3. Call Ordinal_10653 to parse 'uniqueitems' binary table with field descriptors
4. Validate record count <= 0x7FFE (max 32766 unique items)
5. If overflow, abort with error via CleanupAndAbort/ReportError
6. For each unique item record:
   a. Set record index at offset 0x00 (word)
   b. Copy item code to offset 0x02 via Ordinal_10216
   c. Lookup item type via Ordinal_10013, store at offset 0x22
   d. Default type to 0x1507 if lookup fails
7. Store record count in g_adwCrtDataBlock_7

Parameters:
  pDataContext (void*) - Binary data buffer context from game files

Returns:
  void - Table stored in g_adwCrtDataBlock_7 global

Field Descriptors (offset in structure):
  0x00: id (word) - Unique item index
  0x02: name (string) - Item code/name  
  0x22: itemType (word) - Resolved item type ID
  0x24: version (uint) - Game version requirement
  0x28: pattern (string) - Format pattern reference
  0x30: rarity (uint) - Rarity class
  0x34: type (uint) - Type lookup result
  0x36: lvlreq (uint) - Level requirement
  0x38-0x39: transforms (byte) - Char/inv transform indices
  0x3a-0x5a: files (string) - Flippy/inv file references
  0x7c-0x88: cost (uint) - Cost multiplier/add, sounds
  0x8c-0x148: prop1-12 (properties) - Item property arrays

Magic Numbers:
  0x37a - Source line number for allocation
  0x7FFE - Maximum record count (32766)
  0x14c (332) - Record stride in bytes
  0x1507 - Default item type fallback

Error Handling:
  - Overflow: CleanupAndAbort + ReportError(-1) terminates
  - Bad lookup: Uses default type 0x1507

Note: Local variables are FormatDescriptor array entries, not individual locals.

functions.name: CopyStringWithSpacePadding
functions.comment:
Copies up to 4 characters from source string to destination buffer, padding with spaces.

This function implements a fixed-width 4-character string copy commonly used in game
data structures for compact string storage. It reads characters from the source string
until either a null terminator is found or all 4 characters are copied, filling any
remaining destination bytes with space characters (0x20).

Algorithm:
1. Load first character from source string
2. If null terminator found, fill all 4 destination bytes with spaces and return
3. Copy first character to destination byte 0
4. Load second character
5. If null terminator found, fill bytes 1-3 with spaces and return
6. Copy second character to destination byte 1
7. Load third character
8. If null terminator found, fill bytes 2-3 with spaces and return
9. Copy third character to destination byte 2
10. Load fourth character
11. If null terminator found, fill byte 3 with space and return
12. Copy fourth character to destination byte 3
13. Return

Parameters:
  szpSourceString (ECX): Pointer to null-terminated source string
  szpDestBuffer (EAX): Pointer to 4-byte destination buffer for output

Returns:
  void - Destination buffer filled with 4-character string (space-padded)

Special Cases:
  Empty string: All 4 destination bytes filled with spaces (0x20)
  1-3 character string: Characters copied followed by space padding to 4 bytes
  4+ character string: Only first 4 characters copied (no null check on 4th)

functions.name: InitMonsterTypeTable
functions.comment:
Initializes the monster type equivalency table from montype.txt data.

Algorithm:
1. Configure field descriptors for montype.txt parsing (equiv1-3, strsing, strplur columns)
2. Call FOG.Ordinal_10211 to register the data format and field descriptors
3. Call FOG.Ordinal_10653 to parse the montype.txt file and populate record storage
4. Calculate matrix dimensions: stride = (nTypeCount + 31) / 32 DWORDS per row
5. Allocate equivalency matrix: nTypeCount rows * stride DWORDS per row * 4 bytes
6. Zero-fill the allocated equivalency matrix
7. Build equivalency relationships via nested loop:
   - For each monster type i (0 to nTypeCount-1):
     - For each potential equivalent j (0 to nTypeCount-1):
       - Call CheckMonsterTypeEquivalency(i, j) to check if types are equivalent
       - If equivalent, set bit j in row i using bitmask from g_pdwBitMaskTable

Parameters:
  pDataTables - void* IMPLICIT: Pointer to the master data tables context

Returns:

    - g_dwMonTypeTblResHandle: Resource handle for the table
    - g_pMonTypeTblRecords: Pointer to parsed montype.txt records
    - g_nMonTypeCount: Number of monster type entries
    - g_pdwMonTypeEquivMatrix: Bit matrix for equivalency lookups
    - g_nMonTypeEquivStride: DWORD stride per row in equivalency matrix

Special Cases:
  - If nTypeCount is 0, the nested equivalency loop is skipped entirely

functions.name: FindPathToDestination
functions.comment:
Searches for a path from current node to destination using A*-like pathfinding algorithm.

Algorithm:
1. Extract destination coordinates from pPathInput structure
2. Start iteration from current path node (passed via EAX register)
3. For each iteration (max 10000):

   g. Compute heuristic using Manhattan-like distance formula

   i. Allocate new path node from pool (max 900 nodes at offset 0x6274)

functions.name: ParseRoomPresetDataFromStream
functions.comment:
Parses room preset data from a version-controlled binary stream.

This function reads and parses the preset object and monster placement data for a dungeon
room from a raw binary data stream. It handles multiple data format versions (1-18) and
populates the preset context structure with parsed object references, monster spawns,
and tile data pointers.

Algorithm:
1. Read stream header to obtain base pointers and format version
2. Parse dimension counts (width/height) and object counts from header
3. Skip variable-length string data if version >= 3
4. Calculate total entry count based on dimensions
5. For version 9-13, skip 8 bytes of additional header data
6. For version >= 4, parse object pointer arrays into context structure
7. For version < 7, apply object ID remapping from g_adwPresetObjectIdMapping
8. For version >= 2, parse preset object entries:
   a. Read object type (1=monster, 2=item, 3/4=special object)
   b. For type 3+: Search for object code in item data tables
   c. For type 2 (item): Apply act-based offset mapping
   d. For type 1 (monster): Apply monster preset mapping with act offsets
   e. Allocate and populate object entry structure (32 bytes)
9. For version >= 12, parse additional monster spawn data
10. For version >= 14, parse extended tile layer data with sub-entries

Parameters:
  pPresetContext - Pointer to preset context structure receiving parsed data
                   Offsets: +0x00 flags, +0x04 stream ptr, +0x0C height, +0x10 width,
                   +0x14 layer1 count, +0x18 layer2 count, +0x1C-0x48 layer pointers,
                   +0x4C sub-object count, +0x50 sub-object array, +0x54 linked list head
  pRawDataStream - Pointer to raw binary data stream

Returns:
  void - Data written to pPresetContext structure

Special Cases:
  - Version < 4: Uses simplified fixed-offset pointer layout
  - Version 9-13: Contains 8-byte extended header
  - Version >= 16: Contains additional layer2 count field
  - Version >= 18: Skips 4 bytes before sub-object parsing
  - Object ID 0x23D (-1 after mapping): Invalid/skip marker
  - Monster preset acts 0-4: Different lookup tables per act
